acceptedInventoryBaseline.note: Frozen reference values from consume-promote-keep-inventory-v1.json at acceptance. A reclassification recomputes plumbingBaselineLoc = Σ(Consume)+Σ(Promote) over the post-change set; it never re-measures approxLoc/paths (LOC is fixed at baselineCommit). sourceTotalLoc is invariant under any reclassification (a relabel never adds/removes/re-measures source).

versioningConvention: The accepted inventory's '-v1' is immutable. Challenges and reclassifications APPEND an entry to its changeLog and flip only the target row's 'classification' (never approxLoc/paths, never history). A structurally new inventory would be '-v2'. This procedure artifact is itself '-v1'; a structural re-issue would be '-v2'.
noSilentChangeInvariant: For every area whose live 'classification' differs from the value Story 1.4 accepted, there MUST exist a 'reclassification' changeLog entry whose 'to' equals the live value. No live classification may diverge from the accepted baseline without a matching logged entry. In this pilot zero areas differ (the inventory's changeLog is []), so the invariant is vacuously satisfied; the rule is machine-checked the moment Epic 2/3 appends.

challenge.note: A review-time objection to a Consume/Promote/Keep call. An 'upheld' challenge leaves the area's classification UNCHANGED (the entry records that the original call was examined and stands). A 'reclassified' challenge IS a reclassification: it is accompanied by (or upgraded into) a 'reclassification' entry carrying from/to, and obeys the same logging + invariant rules per AC2.

rules: from must equal the area's classification as accepted by Story 1.4 (a reclassification is applied off the accepted baseline)
approxLoc and paths are NOT changed (a misclassification is a boundary/fate correction, not a re-measurement; LOC is fixed at baselineCommit)
the area's live 'classification' is set to 'to' AND this entry justifies it (no-silent-change invariant)

recompute plumbingBaselineLoc = Σ(Consume)+Σ(Promote) over the post-change set; record the result as 'expectedPlumbingAfter' (a Consume<->Promote flip leaves it unchanged; a Keep<->plumbing flip moves it)
if the target area is a promoteLaterCandidate (OQ-3) being flipped to Promote, the rationale MUST record that OQ-3's promote-later boundary was crossed deliberately

workedExamples.rationale: Could the generic check->evidence->verify governance flow be Promoted now (FR-15-adjacent) rather than left Keep-now?
workedExamples.resolutionRationale: OQ-3's promote-later boundary is open. Governance evidence/remediation vocabulary stays Keep-now (promoteLaterCandidate). The hatch records the question and leaves OQ-3 open; it does not dissolve an open question or silently move the row. classification is unchanged; plumbingBaselineLoc stays 13289.

workedExamples.rationale: Worked example per epics Story 2.6 / 3.6 forward-reference ('Commons TypeMapper / NameTypeMapper micro-promote — reclassification logged per Story 1.5'): if Commons cannot satisfy the generic value/identifier converters via the existing public TypeMapper.GetMap() surface, a NameTypeMapper micro-promote is opened additively and the row moves Consume->Promote. Within-plumbing flip: both Consume and Promote count toward plumbing, so plumbingBaselineLoc is unchanged at 13289.

Illustrative Keep<->plumbing flip that exercises the recompute teeth: suppose Story 3.1 finds the IConversationClient/ConversationClientResult surface is in fact generic typed-client plumbing the promoted registration absorbs, not domain surface. Crossing the Keep->plumbing line moves 140 LOC into the plumbing baseline, so plumbingBaselineLoc recomputes from 13289 to 13429 — the move is itself the audit trail SM-1/Story 5.3 reads. This example targets a non-promoteLaterCandidate Keep row, so no OQ-3 boundary is crossed. ILLUSTRATIVE ONLY — not applied to the accepted inventory.
